key_insight: Combining NLP from clinical notes with structured EHR fields uncovered many more social and behavioral health factors linked to frequent ED use in cardiovascular patients than codes or questionnaires alone.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help health systems identify patients with hidden socioeconomic and behavioral risks who are more likely to use the emergency department frequently.
method: Custom NLP extracted 17 social and behavioral determinant domains from unstructured clinical notes.
Structured EHR inputs included ICD-10 Z codes and screening questionnaires.
Multivariable logistic regression tested associations with high ED use (≥5 visits) after adjustment for demographics and chronic conditions.
evidence_signal: In 4,844 adults with cardiovascular disease, 526 (10.9%) were frequent ED users, and note-based NLP identified patients across all 17 domains while increasing prevalence estimates for each domain.
watch_item: Because this was an observational EHR study from one patient cohort, findings may reflect documentation patterns and may not generalize without external validation.
paper_title: Integrating structured and unstructured EHR data to characterize social and behavioral factors associated with frequent emergency department use among patients with cardiovascular disease
